title: The Broken Hollow
premise: Edmund Thornbury has spent his twenty-two years in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot cross its borders and where the last members of the Cartographers' Guild slowly forget their own purpose. When a dying stranger staggers across the border carrying a map that bleeds, Edmund is bound to it by an old guild oath he never swore — and the map pulls him out of the valley into a kingdom where the king has been hollowed out by something ancient wearing his crown. Guided by the stranger's sister, a disgraced royal archivist named Sera, Edmund discovers the map redraws itself as memories are stolen from the land: every place the crown-thing feeds goes blank. To unbind the king, Edmund must offer the one thing magic in this world cannot take without consent — a memory freely given — and he chooses to surrender his memory of the Hollow itself, unmaking his belonging to save a stranger's kingdom. In the end, the king wakes, the crown-thing starves, and Edmund returns home to a valley he remembers only from a map drawn in his own hand.
about_author: Emrys Oyelaran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about the weight of what we choose to remember, and live somewhere they refuse to put on any map.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. We meet the Hollow through its rituals: the guild's dwindling membership, the border stones that hum when magic approaches, and Edmund's secret habit of drawing maps of places he's never seen. His grandmother, the last Master Cartographer, is losing her memory. Emotional beat: quiet suffocation — a life too small for the person living it.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Border Stones
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A man crawls across the border at dusk, bleeding light instead of blood, clutching a folded map that shifts when touched. He presses it into Edmund's hands with an oath-phrase from guild scripture Edmund has never been taught, then dies whispering 'he's still in there.' The map binds itself to Edmund's palm. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant wonder.

chapters.title: What the Map Wants
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, with a brief interlude from the map itself rendered as fragmented first-person text. The map won't release him; it tugs like a current toward the valley's edge. His grandmother recognizes the oath-phrase, goes pale, and tells him the guild didn't make maps of places — it made promises to them. She gives him her compass and her blessing. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Crossing Over
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He steps past the border stones and magic hits him like weather — overwhelming, beautiful, hostile. The map drags him miles in a night to the capital city of Vael, where he's arrested as a spy by guards whose eyes are faintly gray. In his cell he meets Sera, the dead stranger's sister, who recognized the guild seal on his travel papers. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Heresy
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She breaks Edmund out using forgotten maintenance tunnels and shows him the royal archive's sealed wing: records of a king who stopped dreaming three winters ago, and census maps going blank district by district — matching the blanks spreading on Edmund's map. The thing wearing the crown eats memory, and it's eating the kingdom's history to stay fed. Emotional beat: grief for a brother, converted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Blank Districts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Edmund and Sera as they infiltrate a district erased from every record. Its people wander, smiling, unable to say their own names. Edmund realizes the map doesn't just record the thefts — it can restore them, but only if someone holds the memory being restored. He tests this on a child and briefly carries her name for her. Emotional beat: horror tempered by first real agency.

chapters.title: Audience with the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Using Sera's archivist credentials, they gain court access. The king receives them alone; beneath the gray eyes, fragments of the man surface and beg — literally beg — Edmund to finish what his brother started. Guards interrupt; Sera is captured; Edmund escapes with the map burning his hand, now showing a route into the castle's foundations where the crown-thing nests. Emotional beat: guilt and desperation.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Sera's POV, imprisoned, as the crown-thing visits her cell wearing her brother's face, offering her his memories back if she betrays Edmund. Meanwhile Edmund descends beneath the castle and finds the nest: a hoard of stolen names, faces, and years, with the original oath-map at its center — the guild's first promise, broken. Emotional beat: temptation against loyalty; the villain revealed as hunger, not malice.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, climax. He reaches the throne room as the crown-thing prepares to consume the king entirely. The unbinding requires a freely given memory of equal weight to the binding — and Edmund offers the Hollow: his grandmother's voice, the border stones' hum, every year of his small safe life. The crown shatters; the king wakes weeping; the map goes blank except for one valley, drawn in Edmund's own hand. Emotional beat: sacrifice as self-definition.

chapters.title: Home, Redrawn
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, coda. The restored king offers him a place in Vael; Sera offers him something less formal. But Edmund follows the map home, where his grandmother greets a stranger she somehow knows is hers. He begins teaching new guild members that maps are promises, and on the last page of his book he draws the Hollow from memory he no longer has — and finds his hand remembers anyway. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt from choice rather than birthright.
